scenes.b: While Shuka Maharshi was preparing for his journey of wisdom — far away, in a great kingdom, another great story was beginning.
Heir of the Pandava line — a great king who shone in dharma — King Parikshit.
That dharmic king, who looked upon his subjects as his own children — never forgave the arrogant.
One day, on a forest hunt, that king chased a deer far, far away.
The weary king, seized by a fierce thirst, arrived at a nearby ashrama.
A guard mistook a wind-swayed bush for the deer — when the king glanced his way, he hid his sheepish smile.
In the ashrama, Sage Shamika sat — absorbed in deep, silent meditation.
The thirsting king asked for water — but no answer came.
Failing to understand the meditating sage's state — pride quietly crept into the king's heart.
And then, the unknowing mistake — he took the dead snake lying nearby, and placed it around the sage's neck.
Then he turned, and left the ashrama behind.
Shamika's son, Shringi, was at play — when a friend whispered the whole matter to him.
Hearing his father's insult, the boy's heart — blazed with terrible anger.
In his rage, touching the sacred water — the boy pronounced a curse.
The king who insulted my father — within seven days — his death is certain, by the bite of Takshaka!
Lightning flashed in the sky — risen from his silence, Sage Shamika's eyes filled with sorrow.
The sage gently warned — to curse a king who protects his people was a childish act.
At once, he sent his disciple Gauramukha — to carry this news to the king.
As the news arrived — all of Hastinapura fell into silence.
But King Parikshit grieved — not for his death — but for the wrong he had done.
Entrusting the kingdom to his son Janamejaya — he himself renounced the throne.
He reached the bank of the Ganga — resolved to devote his remaining seven days to the divine story.
As he set down the crown, a small ring slipped from his royal jewels onto the path — he did not even look back.
To that bank of the Ganga — the great sages of Bharata began arriving, one by one.
Atri… Vasishtha… Bharadvaja… Gautama — it was as if the whole of India had gathered in one place, in wisdom.
The riverbank transformed into a great assembly of sages.
King Parikshit folded his hands to everyone gathered — and asked a profound question.
O great souls — how should one whose death is near — spend the days that remain?
At that moment — a wondrous light appeared at the edge of the path — a serene young form was approaching.
The beautiful face of a youth — yet the deep silence of self-realization — it was Shukadeva Goswami!
The son of Sage Vyasa — wisdom and detachment in living form — Parikshit rose, and bowed with reverence.
All the sages seated Shuka on the exalted seat — he became the center of the assembly.
Parikshit placed the same question before Shuka — palms joined, his gaze humble.
Shuka smiled softly — O King — this is the right question. For all mortals, the highest good is — hearing the stories of the Lord's glories.
And then, Shuka Maharshi — began to recite the Srimad Bhagavatam.
Those seven days — turned the bank of the Ganga into a divine river of stories.
Every heart was immersed in the story — and time itself stood still.
